intro: General pediatricians have rare clinical skills, so no career outside medicine is a close match. The best fits among the 25 careers below reach only a 61% skill match, led by Industrial-Organizational Psychologists, and most pay much less than the $210,040 pediatricians earn, according to BLS May 2025 data.
why_it_works: Caring for children means examining patients who cannot always explain symptoms, making careful decisions and reassuring worried parents. O*NET rates judgment at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, and complex problem solving and social perceptiveness at 4. Few occupations combine that depth, which is why the matches below are weak. Many pediatricians who step back move into teaching, research or administration.
tips: Part-time or locum work keeps your license and income while you explore other options.
Clinical research coordination is a 59% match with a median of $167,220 for its broader group.
Teaching roles in medical schools are not separate careers in this data; ask your hospital about academic posts.

faq.q: What jobs can former pediatricians do?
faq.a: The closest matches by skills are Industrial-Organizational Psychologists (61%), clinical research coordinators (59%) and Genetic Counselors (56%), based on O*NET 31.0. These are weak matches, and many pediatricians who leave practice stay in medicine through teaching, research or public health roles.

faq.q: Which careers for pediatricians pay more?
faq.a: Only 1 of the 25 matches pays more: Chief Executives earn $213,990, which is 2% more, though the match is only 47%. Industrial-Organizational Psychologists earn $193,950, which is 8% less, and need their own graduate training, according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do pediatricians need more education to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than pediatricians already have, including all of the top 10. A master's degree is common in close matches, held by 58% of workers in one, so your medical degree more than covers the formal requirements.

faq.q: What skills would pediatricians need for a new career?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, instructing, operation and control and programming. Service orientation already rates 3.88 out of 5 for pediatricians in O*NET, so teaching and organizational skills are the most realistic directions outside clinical care.
